newsitem.title: FALKLAND ISLANDS: Britain wants Menem to visit London, but not yet.
newsitem.headline: Britain wants Menem to visit London, but not yet.

text.p: Britain still wants Argentine President Carlos Menem to visit London but the time is not yet right, a senior Foreign Office official said on Tuesday.
"The British government will be glad to see President Menem in London but the appropriate moment hasn't yet been seen to proceed," the official, Robert Burns, told a news conference.
He was speaking after a three-day visit to the disputed Falkland Islands, over which Britain fought a bloody war with Argentina in 1982.
British Prime Minister John Major invited Menem to visit when the two leaders met in New York at the United Nations general assembly in September last year.

The invitation marked a mending of relations after the Falklands War but relations have been under strain recently over fishing rights in the waters around the islands, known in Argentina as Las Malvinas.
Burns said Britain was "anxious to finalise a long-term fisheries agreement" with Argentina.

He said Britain was not prepared to make any concessions on the islands' sovereignty, adding that the government wanted "a good and harmonious relationship with Argentina but this will not be at the expense of the Falklands."
